triggers: a Metal kernel risks the 'writing b fragments via thread_elements() with a guessed layout produces wrong numerics' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on Apple M-series Metal: writing b fragments via thread_elements() with a guessed layout produces wrong numerics

problem.target: Apple Silicon (M-series) unified-memory GPU, Metal 4 toolchains
problem.statement: writing b fragments via thread_elements() with a guessed layout produces wrong numerics

payload.attempted: Three independent experiments: (1) read-back probe; (2) register-side B dequant under two documented layout assumptions; (3) minimal MMA probe that builds fragment B via thread_elements() under 4 candidate layouts and runs one 8x8 MMA against a known A - all 4 variants output an all-zero product matrix (maxerr 140 = every element wrong).
payload.lesson: Treat simdgroup fragments as opaque: stage through threadgroup memory with simdgroup_load/store. Sizing the MLX gap: with public APIs the practical ceiling observed is ~9 TFLOPS effective for q4 GEMM (33.2ms qkv shape) versus MLX ~43 TFLOPS; closing further needs Apple-internal primitives or upstream toolchain changes.

established_fact.mechanism: On the metal4.0 toolchain (metalfe-32023.921.6), thread_elements() returns storage whose contents never influence simdgroup MMA inputs or reflect loaded fragment state - the accessor is effectively disconnected. Register-side dequantization into MMA fragments requires either documented layout-stable APIs or privileged Apple primitives.

payload.observed: (2) correctness failures max_abs 1.1-3.6; (3) MMA product all zeros for layouts 0-3. simdgroup_load/store round trips through threadgroup memory remain correct and fast.
payload.root_cause: The per-thread element mapping of simdgroup_matrix fragments is not stable API on this toolchain: thread_elements() read-back returns zeros and neither documented layout matches hardware placement, so register-side dequant cannot be verified cheaply.
